tokyo_lambiance_douce_higashiueno.gf_detail: GF — ask: no gluten-free statement. Lunch comes with bread (one free refill) and dinner has a bread-and-service charge; the sauces (cream, mustard cream, Lyonnaise, red wine) are not described.
tokyo_lambiance_douce_higashiueno.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a pork-led bistro — charcuterie, pâté, roast and braised pork, duck, beef, gizzard confit, cream and cheese; no vegan dish is named.
tokyo_lambiance_douce_higashiueno.hours_raw: Tue, Wed, Fri, Sat 11:30–14:30 (food last order 13:30) and 18:00–22:30 (food last order 20:00, drinks 22:00); Thu dinner only 18:00–22:30; closed Mondays and Sundays (Tabelog). How to book: phone 03-6284-2962, best after 14:30; lunch can be booked only on Saturdays and public holidays, by phone; groups of five or more by phone only. Weekday lunch is first come, first served — about 10 people were already queuing before the 11:30 opening in October 2026. Dinner: ¥500 per person for bread and service; at least one drink per person; no children under junior-high age. 19 seats (16 at tables, 3 at the counter). Non-smoking. Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners) and PayPay; no e-money. Opened 1 November 2017.
tokyo_lambiance_douce_higashiueno.notes: [French bistro · Naka-Okachimachi, the one-person bistro with the lunch queue] A small, warm French bistro between Ueno and Okachimachi, open since 2017, best known for generous ¥1,650 lunches: salad with a spicy carrot râpé, bread, and a choice of four mains such as a coarse French-style hamburger (steak haché) with mustard cream sauce, braised pork shank, or pork belly with sauerkraut. Reviewers keep remarking that one person cooks and serves everything smoothly. Weekday lunch is first come, first served, and about ten people were already queuing before the 11:30 opening in October 2026; Saturday lunch is booked by phone. Dinner is a wine bistro — charcuterie, pâté, roast pork from Kochi, duck, beef cheek — with a ¥500 bread-and-service charge, one drink per person, and no young children.

chef_bio.background: Reviews from September–October 2026 say the owner runs the restaurant alone; at an October 2026 dinner for six, a second server was helping. No source names the owner.
chef_bio.philosophy: Per the listing, the menu is made to go with wine, so dishes may taste strong without alcohol; at dinner, at least one drink per person is asked.
chef_bio.specialty: Pork dishes; steak haché lunch.

anecdotes.text: "Despite being a one-person operation, the service was smooth, and I didn't feel like I was waiting at all." — October 2026.

tokyo_koiki_soba_inaricho.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: soba in a soy-based broth with wheat-batter tempura, plus ramen and champon with wheat noodles; the soba is not described as pure buckwheat.
tokyo_koiki_soba_inaricho.vegan_detail: Not vegan: the soba broth is a dashi (reviews praise the dashi flavour), and toppings include shrimp, squid and egg; even the vegetable tempura soba sits in that broth.
tokyo_koiki_soba_inaricho.hours_raw: Mon–Fri 7:30–16:00 and 17:00–1:00; closed Saturdays and Sundays (Tabelog, a user-built listing — "accuracy cannot be guaranteed"). Reviews differ: a September 2026 diner ate there on a Saturday around noon, with one staff member instead of the usual two; an August 2026 diner was told it opened at 17:00 on Sunday, but found it closed. From 17:00 it runs as an izakaya with smartphone ordering (September 2026). No reservations. Tickets from a machine. No cards; e-money accepted. 20 seats (12 at the counter, 8 at tables). Smoking area; no smoking 11:00–14:00.
tokyo_koiki_soba_inaricho.notes: [Soba · Inaricho, a station-side soba counter from 7:30 am to 1 am] A no-frills soba shop right by Exit 3 of Inaricho Station, with tickets from a machine and food out in seconds. The menu runs far past plain soba: vegetable tempura soba for ¥550, gesoten (squid-leg tempura) soba, rice-bowl sets, and an unusual shoyu ramen made with the soba dipping sauce (¥550; a September 2026 reviewer said fans of Kansai-style broth ramen will like it), plus Omi Champon. From 17:00 it turns into a small izakaya with phone ordering, highballs and squid tempura. Tabelog says closed at weekends, but reviewers in 2026 found it open on a Saturday and closed on a Sunday — check before going at the weekend. No smoking only from 11:00 to 14:00.

chef_bio.background: Tabelog listing built by users ("accuracy cannot be guaranteed"); usually two staff on weekdays, one on a Saturday (September 2026). No source names the owner or opening date.
chef_bio.specialty: Tempura soba; gesoten soba; ramen made with soba sauce.

anecdotes.text: "The noodles were chewy and delicious, even better than some ramen shops." — October 2026, shoyu ramen ¥550 (large +¥100).
"This ramen uses the dipping sauce from a soba shop. The sweet broth is prominent and quite delicious." — September 2026, large shoyu ramen ¥650.
"The soba remained firm even in the hot dipping sauce, making this place a great choice for warm soba." — September 2026, shrimp tempura rice bowl set.
"I thought it was a vending machine, but it turns out to be a smartphone ordering izakaya." — September 2026, from 17:00.

tokyo_soba_shin_ueno.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: the soba is a 2:8 blend (eight parts domestic buckwheat to two parts other flour, per the menu and an August 2026 review), served with soy-based dipping sauces.
tokyo_soba_shin_ueno.vegan_detail: Not vegan: every dipping sauce is built on bonito (katsuobushi) dashi, some with chicken paitan or milk, and most bowls come with miso-marinated pork chashu.
tokyo_soba_shin_ueno.hours_raw: Mon–Fri 11:30–14:00 and 17:00–22:00; Sat 11:00–20:30; Sun 11:00–19:30; public holidays 11:00–20:00 (Tabelog). An August 2026 review said it was open into the evening only on Saturdays; Tabelog lists weekday evenings too. No reservations. Tickets from a machine at the entrance; fully cashless (cards, transport IC, PayPay, Alipay and more). 11 seats (7 at the counter, 4 at a table). Non-smoking. Children welcome. Opened 7 July 2025.
tokyo_soba_shin_ueno.notes: [Soba · Ueno-Hirokoji, creative dipping soba from a Ginza kitchen] A clean, modern soba counter between Ueno and Okachimachi, opened in July 2025 by the Ginza Japanese restaurant Kurahashi. It works like a ramen shop — buy a ticket at the machine (cashless only), sit at the counter — but the noodles are 2:8 domestic buckwheat, praised for texture and aroma, and the dipping sauces start from bonito dashi: sesame-vinegar seafood, a creamy milk chicken-paitan with cheese, soy-milk tantan, grilled miso, and spicy mala. A slice of miso-marinated pork chashu is grilled at the counter just before serving and is what several reviewers single out. Plain zaru soba is ¥850; most bowls are ¥1,000–1,150, and a September 2026 reviewer urges adding the kayaku rice. Tabelog lists an English menu.

chef_bio.background: Per the Tabelog listing (official information), a new soba concept from Kurahashi, a Japanese restaurant in Ginza, with dashi made by its chefs; an August 2026 review also says it is run by "Ginza Kurahashi". No source names the chef in Ueno.
chef_bio.specialty: Dipping soba with grilled miso-marinated chashu.

anecdotes.text: "Made with 80/20 buckwheat flour, it has great texture, aroma, and a smooth finish—definitely better than your average neighborhood soba shop." — August 2026, mazesoba.
"What left the biggest impression on me was the grilled miso-marinated chashu!" — September 2026, grilled miso dipping soba.

tokyo_sogen_no_ie_higashiueno.gf_detail: GF — ask: much of the menu is wheat — homemade noodles, shumai, gyoza, Khoshuur (fried meat pies), lamb udon; grilled skewers, salt-boiled spare ribs and salads are not described as gluten-free, and some stir-fries are soy-sauce based.
tokyo_sogen_no_ie_higashiueno.vegan_detail: Vegan — ask: a lamb, beef and milk menu; a few vegetable dishes (tofu salad, smashed cucumber, stir-fried shredded potato, stir-fried bean sprouts and pea shoots) are listed, but the seasonings and stock are not described.
tokyo_sogen_no_ie_higashiueno.hours_raw: Mon, Wed–Sun, public holidays 11:30–15:00 and 17:00–22:00; closed Tuesdays; closing days may vary (Tabelog). Reservations taken (Tabelog, phone or online); an August 2026 review says it often fills up. Appetizer charge ¥280 per person (Tabelog; a July 2026 diner paid ¥300 for the meat appetizer). Courses with all-you-can-drink for 3–20 people: ¥2,980 (90 min), ¥3,980 (120 min), ¥4,980 (180 min). Ordering by QR code (October 2026). Take-out and delivery. 20 seats (tables). tokyo_sogen_no_ie_higashiueno.notes: [Mongolian · Naka-Okachimachi, lamb and shumai under a ger-style ceiling] A small, slightly hard-to-find Mongolian restaurant between Okachimachi and Ueno, decorated like a ger, with a ceiling that tints photos blue. The cooking is lamb-led and simply seasoned: steamed lamb shumai served in a bamboo basket, Khoshuur (fried lamb pies), cumin lamb skewers, Khorkhog, stuffed lamb stomach, lamb soup with homemade noodles, and homemade yogurt. Lunch sets cost about ¥800–1,100 (2024 prices); dinner runs ¥3,000–4,000 with Mongolian beers, salty milk tea, vodka and camel-milk liquor. Reviewers in 2025–2026 mostly found it authentic and generous; one in September 2026 found it toned down and the portions small. It was previously listed as モンゴル焼売 and renamed after a change of owner (Forbes Japan, June 2024).

chef_bio.origin: At this address, a shop listed as モンゴル焼売 (Mongolian shumai) changed owners and was renamed 草原の家 (Forbes Japan, 26 June 2024).
chef_bio.background: Tabelog official listing; per the listing, guests can chat with the owner. Two staff on a busy July 2026 evening — one in the dining room, one in the kitchen. No source names the owner or cooks.
chef_bio.specialty: Handmade shumai and gyoza; lamb spare ribs (Tabelog listing).

tokyo_salsa_cabana_bar_yotsuya.gf_detail: Ask. One June 2026 diner noted the taco shells are corn-based rather than fried wheat, but burritos, shrimp fritters and nachos are also on the menu and nothing is called gluten-free.
tokyo_salsa_cabana_bar_yotsuya.vegan_detail: Ask. Guacamole, avocado salsa salad and tomato salsa are plant-based in principle; tacos are filled with beef, chicken or pork and much of the menu has cheese.
tokyo_salsa_cabana_bar_yotsuya.hours_raw: Mon–Fri 17:00–24:00; Sat, Sun and holidays 15:00–24:00 (from August 2026); last order 23:00; closed over New Year; ask about lunch (Tabelog; official site). Reservations by phone, Tabelog (confirmed by a call back) or Google Maps (October 2026); one drink per person (October 2025). 20 seats, tables close together, open terrace; whole-shop hire up to 20; non-smoking (Tabelog; September 2026). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX), Suica, iD, QUICPay and QR (Tabelog). Takeaway and delivery (official site).
tokyo_salsa_cabana_bar_yotsuya.notes: [Mexican · Yotsuya, a taco and mojito bar off Shinmichi-dōri] A small, Mexican-decorated bar a minute from Yotsuya Station, one of two Salsa Cabana shops (the other is in Nakano), where the menu leans on ingredients brought in from Mexico. Diners in 2026 came for hand-rolled tacos with chewy, fragrant tortillas, guacamole and avocado salsa, skirt-steak skewers that sold out on a busy weekend, and a long list of mojitos and tequila. An October 2026 visitor writes that it was among the first restaurants in Japan to receive the Mexican government's Sello M mark for authentic Mexican cuisine. Weekends get packed and loud, tables are tight, and it works best for a casual round or a second stop; open to midnight, from 15:00 at weekends.

chef_bio.origin: Yotsuya shop of Salsa Cabana, which also runs a Nakano shop (official site); "Grill Cabana" and "Salsa Cabana" merged as "Salsa Cabana Bar" (Tabelog).
chef_bio.background: No source names the owner or cooks; a 2021 note in a September 2026 review mentions "friendly young staff members and a pleasant owner". Official site: Latin atmosphere with Mexican text throughout the interior; many ingredients and seasonings imported from Mexico; Mexican beer, homemade sangria and tequila cocktails; catering. An October 2026 diner: "I visited one of Japan's first certified establishments" of the Sello M programme run by the Mexican Ministry of Foreign Affairs with the Mexican Culinary Academy.
chef_bio.philosophy: Flavours and aromas that only Mexican ingredients can give (official site).
chef_bio.specialty: Hand-rolled tacos; mojitos.

anecdotes.text: "The tacos were made with a corn-based shell instead of a fried wheat one. The aftertaste was fragrant and sweet, making them quite addictive." — June 2026.
"I visited one of Japan's first certified establishments, Salsa Cabana in Yotsuya, with two friends… Reservations can be made through Google Maps." — October 2026.
"I ended up having about 4.5 glasses, refilling each time." — September 2026, mojitos at an after-party.

Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners); no e-money or QR (Tabelog). English menu; sommelier (Tabelog).
tokyo_sushi_koruri_yotsuya.notes: [Sushi · Yotsuya, a ten-seat counter in Comore with sake pairings] A dim, cobalt-blue-accented ten-seat counter on the ground floor of the Comore Yotsuya complex, where a chef with 30 years' experience serves omakase built for drinking: the shop pours small tastes of sake and wine and keeps about 200 bottles. Diners in 2025–26 praised the side dishes as much as the nigiri — stacked chutoro, simmered abalone with liver sauce turned into a little risotto, sea-urchin and toro hand rolls — at ¥18,000–30,000, less than Ginza would charge, one 2024 diner reckoned. You need not all start at once. On Wednesday to Friday lunch there are just two red-vinegar bowls, a ten-topping bara chirashi for ¥3,000 and a tuna bowl for ¥3,800. Saturday 17:00–19:00 is a family slot for parents with small children. One 2024 diner found dishes arriving too fast; no requests for allergies.

chef_bio.background: Tabelog (corporate-member listing): "With over 30 years of experience, our chef carefully selects high-quality ingredients"; sake and wine pairings in small tastings; around 200 bottled wines; cobalt-blue glassware. A February 2026 reviewer writes that the shop "is actually part of the Marugo Group". No source names the chef. Reviews dated from July 2024 call the building new.
chef_bio.philosophy: Craftsmanship, carefully chosen ingredients and quality time (Tabelog).
chef_bio.specialty: Omakase with sake pairing; bara chirashi lunch.

anecdotes.text: "With only 10 counter seats, it's nice that you can enter at your preferred time rather than all at once… the full course includes an impressive 11 types of sake." — November 2025.
"This was my second visit with my grandfather… While the sushi was exceptional, the side dishes were truly outstanding." — March 2026.
"The Bara Chirashi includes about ten different toppings… The sushi rice is made with red vinegar." — February 2026, weekday lunch.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ (店舗会員): 鮨 こるり、寿司・日本酒バー・ワインバー、四谷1-6-1 コモレ四谷1F、四ツ谷駅から徒歩3分、火18:00〜23:00、水〜金11:30〜13:30・18:00〜23:00、土17:00〜23:00 (毎週土曜はファミリーデー17:00〜19:00)、日月休み、食材の指定やアレルギーには対応できない、ランチは事前注文がないと売り切れることも、サービス料なし、10席 (貸切12名)、禁煙、カード可、英語メニュー、ソムリエ、経験30年以上の職人、日本酒やワインを少量で、ボトルワイン約200種、コバルトブルーの小さなグラス。口コミ(2024年7月〜2026年3月): 8,000円の握りのコースから30,000円のフルコース (日本酒11種)、18,000円のコース、中トロの5枚重ね、鮑の肝ソース、昼は水木金のみでばらちらし3,000円と鮪丼3,800円、赤酢、プリンのような玉子焼き、まるごグループという声。

tokyo_wines_by_california_neuf_yotsuya.gf_detail: Ask. Lunch is only couscous (wheat; one February 2026 diner was served quinoa instead) with a quiche Lorraine, and dinner has quiche, pâté and fried corn fritters; the steaks and confits are not described for gluten.
tokyo_wines_by_california_neuf_yotsuya.vegan_detail: Ask. The couscous stew is lamb (with beef in one 2026 account) and the quiche has bacon; homemade pickles and the vegetables are the plant items named.
tokyo_wines_by_california_neuf_yotsuya.hours_raw: Mon–Fri lunch 12:00–14:30 (last order 14:00) and dinner 17:00–23:00 (last order 22:30); closed Saturday, Sunday and holidays (Tabelog). Lunch can sell out (May 2025). Table charge ¥330 (Tabelog). 15 seats: 5 at the counter, three tables for two and one for four; non-smoking; private hire possible (Tabelog). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners); no e-money or QR (Tabelog). Opened December 2016 (May 2025 review).
tokyo_wines_by_california_neuf_yotsuya.notes: [French · Yotsuya, a California-wine bistro with a couscous lunch] Up on the second floor of a quiet building toward the back of Shinmichi-dōri, a 15-seat bistro in navy and dark wood, open since 2016, pouring more than 80 California wines with French bistro cooking. Weekday lunch is one dish only and a cult favourite: a freshly baked quiche Lorraine with salad, then couscous under a spiced lamb-and-vegetable stew, refilled if you ask, with harissa on the side, for about ¥1,100 — one diner logged 30 visits. In the evening it is a calm wine bar where solo guests are welcome: sliced prosciutto, house oil sardines, gizzard confit with raisins, outside-skirt steak with fries, and glasses of Napa wine from about ¥800. Closed weekends; ¥330 table charge.

chef_bio.background: No source names the owner or cooks; a May 2025 diner was greeted by "the owner" with a warm "Welcome!". Tabelog: over 80 carefully selected California wines; signature quiche; sommelier available.
chef_bio.specialty: Couscous lunch with quiche; California wines.

anecdotes.text: "I'm sad to think about how many more times I can visit now that I'm leaving Yotsuya… the quiche and couscous were consistently delicious." — March 2026, a 29th visit.
"Unlike the couscous typically found in France, the vegetables here are not stewed but rather served fresh… You can have as much ragu as you like." — March 2026, lunch.
"I was particularly surprised by how well the raisins paired with the confit gizzards." — April 2025, solo at 17:00.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ: Wines By California Neuf、ビストロ・ワインバー・ダイニングバー、四谷1-20 岩井第一ビル2F、四ツ谷駅から徒歩3分、月〜金12:00〜14:30 (L.O.14:00)・17:00〜23:00 (L.O.22:30)、土日祝休み、テーブルチャージ330円、15席 (カウンター5、2人がけ3卓、4人がけ1卓)、禁煙、カード可、ソムリエ、カリフォルニアワイン80種以上、名物のキッシュ、ハラミステーキ、イベリコ豚、鴨のコンフィ、クスクス。口コミ(2025年2月〜2026年9月): ランチはクスクスのみ1,100〜1,200円、キッシュロレーヌとサラダ、仔羊と野菜の煮込み、おかわり可、ハリッサ、夜は生ハム660円、自家製オイルサーディン770円、砂肝のコンフィ、ハラミとフライドポテト、コーンのフリット、グラスワイン800円ほどから、2016年12月オープン。

cultural_comfort.note: One-dish lunch; at night ask the sommelier for a California wine.

tokyo_gyoza_sakaba_yotsuya.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: gyoza in wheat wrappers, noodle dishes (tantanmen, yakisoba, cold noodles) and soy-based Chinese sauces; nothing gluten-free is described.
tokyo_gyoza_sakaba_yotsuya.vegan_detail: Ask. The listing ticks "Vegetarian options", but the gyoza are meat- or seafood-filled and no vegan dish is named.
tokyo_gyoza_sakaba_yotsuya.hours_raw: Daily 11:00–15:00 and 17:00–23:00 (Tabelog). Reservations taken; no booking needed for most lunches (2026 reviews). 50 seats: 16 on the ground floor (counter and tables), 34 in the basement with semi-private tables; hire for 20–50+; smoking allowed (Tabelog). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners) (Tabelog); PayPay accepted (June 2026). Takeaway (Tabelog).
tokyo_gyoza_sakaba_yotsuya.notes: [Gyoza · Yotsuya, a two-floor gyoza and Chinese tavern on Shinmichi-dōri] A plain, roomy gyoza house over two floors on Shinmichi-dōri, open every day for lunch and dinner, that keeps going when the street's smaller places are full. Lunch is the draw for 2026 office workers: a set of fried rice and six gyoza for ¥930, or tantanmen, Taiwanese ramen or the daily special with half fried rice for ¥980, with almond tofu to finish and free rice refills, usually served within ten minutes. At night it turns tavern: three-kind gyoza platters, crisp spicy chicken wings, mapo tofu and seafood yakisoba with beer. Reviews call the food solid rather than special and the service brisk to curt. Smoking is allowed.

chef_bio.background: No source names the owner or cooks; Tabelog gives no opening date. A web search found a shop of the same name in Kachidoki, not confirmed as related.
chef_bio.philosophy: "Enjoy delicious food and stay healthy" (Tabelog, machine-translated).
chef_bio.specialty: Gyoza; spicy chicken wings.

anecdotes.text: "The weekly special menu features Taiwanese ramen with half fried rice for JPY 980… From entering the restaurant to finishing my meal took less than 30 minutes." — August 2026, a fourth visit.
"The gyoza were delicious with a thin skin and generous filling. The shrimp gyoza had a nice crunch from the shrimp." — July 2026, ¥4,400 with beer.
"Just when I was feeling lost, I stumbled upon this place… It seems like a reliable spot to turn to when in need." — October 2026, Friday night.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ: 餃子酒場 四谷本店、中華料理・餃子・四川料理、四谷1-19 アーバン四谷ビルB1F〜1F、JR・地下鉄四ツ谷駅2番出口から徒歩2分、毎日11:00〜15:00・17:00〜23:00、50席 (1F 16席、B1 34席、半個室あり)、喫煙可、カード可、テイクアウト、外はパリッと中はジューシーな餃子、甘辛の手羽先。口コミ(2025年10月〜2026年10月): 炒飯と焼き餃子6個930円 (杏仁豆腐付き)、担々麺や台湾ラーメンと半炒飯980円、日替わり定食980円 (ご飯おかわり自由)、麻婆豆腐定食、海老餃子、餃子3種盛り、手羽先、海鮮あんかけ焼きそば、胡麻団子、PayPay 可、接客はそっけないという声。

tokyo_koho_roppongi.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: a set course with dumplings, shumai, xiaolongbao, kadaif-wrapped shrimp and Hong Kong noodles (October 2026).
tokyo_koho_roppongi.vegan_detail: Not vegan: set courses of duck, chicken, seafood, ham and shark fin.
tokyo_koho_roppongi.hours_raw: Daily: lunch 12:00–14:00 (food last order 12:00), dinner 18:00–22:00 (food last order 20:00) (Tabelog). Phone before 15:00. Courses only, booked ahead. 10% service charge, included in course prices. 14 seats, counter only; private hire up to 20. Non-smoking. No children. Please do not wear perfume. Cards, e-money and QR (PayPay, Alipay, WeChat Pay and others). Dishes use alcohol — say so when booking if you cannot have it; no changes after arrival. Reopened here 28 May 2026 (Tabelog) after moving within Roppongi.
tokyo_koho_roppongi.notes: [Chinese · Roppongi, a 20-small-plate Cantonese–Sichuan counter] A dark, stage-like 14-seat counter in a back alley off Enma-zaka, which moved here in May 2026. Koho serves Chinese food as a long run of small plates — 20 dishes in the ¥15,800 Signature Course — mixing Cantonese technique, Sichuan heat and Japanese seasonal produce: Peking duck wrapped with apple instead of cucumber, a steamer of three dim sum, chicken wings stuffed with foie gras and buried in chillies, Omi duck with black vinegar and Shine Muscat, and a shark-fin clay-pot rice to finish. Diners in 2026 praised the variety and the value for the level; one reviewer says the shop opened in 2016 and pioneered this small-plate style. Lunch omakase ¥9,800; no children, no perfume.

chef_bio.chef_name: Yuki Kaneko (executive chef, as written in the Tabelog shop text)
roles: Executive chef (Tabelog shop text)
chef_bio.background: Per the Tabelog shop text, executive chef Yuki Kaneko graduated from the Osaka Abeno Tsuji Culinary Institute, learned Chinese cooking at Heichinrou, then at the one-star SENSE at the Mandarin Oriental Tokyo, and was head chef at Series in Azabudai, which gained a Michelin star eight months after opening and kept it five years in a row. An October 2026 reviewer was welcomed by "Chef Kato Kazuaki, who took over after the move". Another October 2026 reviewer says Koho opened in 2016, is a regular Tabelog Award winner and moved in May 2026. The name joins "tiger" (a talent) and "peak" (Tabelog shop text).
chef_bio.philosophy: Nurture talent and aim for the highest peak; Cantonese delights with the excitement of Sichuan, one plate at a time (Tabelog shop text).
chef_bio.specialty: Small-plate Cantonese–Sichuan course; Peking duck with apple.

anecdotes.text: "The Peking duck was delicious, paired with apples instead of the usual cucumber, showcasing a refreshing twist." — October 2026, Signature Course ¥15,800.
"It’s very hot, but if you can handle it, definitely try it fresh out of the fryer!" — October 2026, chicken wing with foie gras.
"The dishes were served in small portions, allowing for a delightful experience, and each dish was original and incredibly delicious." — October 2026, first visit since the move.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ (店舗会員): 虎峰、港区六本木3-14-16 ペンタビル1F、大江戸線六本木駅5番出口から徒歩5分、日比谷線3番出口から8分、毎日12:00〜14:00、18:00〜22:00、サービス料10%、14席 (カウンターのみ)、貸切20名まで、禁煙、子ども不可、香水は控える、カード・電子マネー・QR可、2026年5月28日オープン。店の紹介: 広東料理の技に四川の刺激、世界のエッセンス、総料理長 Yuki Kaneko (Tsuji の学校、Heichinrou、SENSE、Series)、ワインとお茶のペアリング。コース: 昼のおまかせ9,800円、Premium Course 25,800円、クリスマス33,000円。口コミ(2026年9月〜10月): シグネチャーコース20品15,800円、北京ダックはりんごで、点心3種、手羽先のフォアグラ詰め、鴨の黒酢、ふかひれの土鍋ご飯、移転後の料理長は Kato Kazuaki という声。

cultural_comfort.note: Set courses at the counter; book ahead.

tokyo_bangkok_roppongi.gf_detail: Ask. Many dishes are rice or rice noodles, but Pad See Ew is seasoned with soy sauce (October 2026) and nothing is called gluten-free.
tokyo_bangkok_roppongi.vegan_detail: Ask. Tabelog lists vegetarian options, but the lunch dishes are chicken, pork or shrimp and no vegan dishes are described.
tokyo_bangkok_roppongi.hours_raw: Mon–Sat 11:30–14:30 (last order 14:00) and 17:00–23:00 (last order 22:00); closed Sundays (Tabelog). Lunch is cash only (two July 2026 reviews); Tabelog lists cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners, UnionPay), no e-money or QR. Busy at lunch, with a queue at times (July 2026). 28 seats at tables; private hire for 20–50. Non-smoking. Children and strollers welcome. Takeout. Staff from overseas who speak good Japanese (July 2026).
tokyo_bangkok_roppongi.notes: [Thai · Roppongi, a 35-year-old Thai restaurant with ¥1,100 lunch sets] On the second floor of a building in a Roppongi back alley, a calm, homely 28-seat room that has served Thai food for more than 35 years. Lunch is the draw: ¥1,100 for green curry, Gapao rice with a fried egg, Tom Yum noodles or the half-and-half of Gapao and green curry, each with soup, salad and dessert — and a mini curry for ¥200 more. Diners in 2026 call it authentic, properly spicy and excellent value; one found the green curry a little salty. In the evening there is soft-shell crab curry, Tom Yum Goong and courses from ¥3,000. Lunch is cash only; closed Sundays.

chef_bio.background: The Tabelog shop text describes more than 35 years of authentic flavours preserved by chefs of the Thai Embassy, with lighter dishes too. July 2026 diners describe staff from overseas who speak good Japanese and are attentive. No one is named in the sources read.
chef_bio.philosophy: Authentic, colourful Thai food in a homely space, with lighter dishes for those who avoid heavy ethnic food (Tabelog shop text).
chef_bio.specialty: Half-and-half Gapao and green curry lunch.

anecdotes.text: "The Gapao had a solid spiciness, with the aroma of basil and a zesty flavor that made the rice irresistible." — July 2026, half-and-half lunch.
"A great perk is that for an additional JPY 200, you can add a mini Green Curry or mini Gapao Rice." — July 2026.
"The green curry was a bit salty, but it was fine for summer." — July 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ (店舗会員): バンコク、港区六本木3-8-8 六本木ＷＯＯビル2F、六本木駅5番出口から徒歩2分、月〜土11:30〜14:30 (L.O.14:00)、17:00〜23:00 (L.O.22:00)、日休み、28席 (テーブル)、貸切20〜50名、禁煙、カード可、子ども・ベビーカー可、テイクアウト、ベジタリアンメニューあり。店の紹介: 35年以上続く、タイ大使館のシェフが守ってきた本場の味、Light Course 6品3,000円などのコース。口コミ(2026年6月〜10月): 昼は1,100円 (大盛り1,200円) でスープ、サラダ、デザート付き、Gapao とグリーンカレーのハーフ&ハーフ、ミニカレー+200円、昼は現金のみ、Pad See Ew、夜はソフトシェルクラブのカレー、Tom Yum Goong、海外出身で日本語の上手なスタッフ。

cultural_comfort.note: Staff from overseas who speak good Japanese (July 2026).

tokyo_ajiman_roppongi.gf_detail: Ask. Fugu sashimi is eaten with house ponzu and a liver sauce, and the menu includes kara-age (2026 reviews); nothing is said about gluten.
tokyo_ajiman_roppongi.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a fugu restaurant — sashimi, kara-age, hot pot and zosui of fugu.
tokyo_ajiman_roppongi.hours_raw: 18:00–24:00 (Tabelog). Seasonal: closed in July and August; open every day from September to March; closed Sundays from April to June; hours may change, so check first (Tabelog). Reviewers nonetheless report visits in July 2026. Reservations by referral only — no first-time bookings, and only regular customers can book (2025–2026 reviews). Cash only: no cards, e-money or QR. 12 seats at the counter plus tatami private rooms for 2 to 20; whole-shop hire up to 20. Non-smoking. À la carte or an omakase course; about ¥40,000–¥100,000 a head in reviews.
tokyo_ajiman_roppongi.notes: [Fugu · Roppongi, a referral-only fugu house since 1981] An old-fashioned, Showa-feeling fugu restaurant in a Roppongi back alley — a counter and tatami rooms — that has served pufferfish since 1981 and won Tabelog Award Silver in 2026. Wild fugu of around 1.8 kg is aged and cut into famously thick sashimi, eaten with kabosu ponzu or a rich liver sauce, followed by grilled shirako, huge fugu kara-age, hot pot and zosui, with hirezake throughout. Regulars come back season after season, some more than twenty times. Bookings are by referral only — new guests cannot reserve — and it is cash only. Closed in July and August, and on Sundays from April to June, per Tabelog.

chef_bio.background: Established in 1981 (March and May 2026 reviews). A May 2026 reviewer calls it family-run and says it once held a Michelin star. Regulars mention chatting with the chef and the owner at the counter (July 2026). The Tabelog Award: Silver 2019, 2020, 2022 and 2026; Bronze 2021, 2023, 2024 and 2025 (Tabelog). No one is named in the sources read.
chef_bio.specialty: Thick-cut wild fugu sashimi with liver sauce; fugu kara-age.

anecdotes.text: "It turns out that only regular customers can make reservations now, and if you're not on the list, you can't book a table." — June 2025 visit.
"Dipping the fugu sashimi in that rich liver sauce is truly blissful. The slices are thick and incredibly satisfying." — March 2026.
"The fried fugu was juicy, comparable to fried chicken, it was unbelievably delicious." — April 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ: 味満ん、港区六本木3-8-8 ＷＯＯビル1F、六本木駅から10分、18:00〜24:00、7月と8月は休み、9月〜3月は無休、4月〜6月は日曜休み、変わることもあるので要確認、カード・電子マネー・QR不可、12席、個室 (2〜20名)、座敷、貸切20名まで、禁煙、The Tabelog Award Silver 2019・2020・2022・2026、Bronze 2021・2023・2024・2025。口コミ(2025年〜2026年7月): 1981年創業、紹介のみで新規の予約は不可、現金のみ、厚切りのてっさ、肝の漬けだれ、かぼすの自家製ポン酢、白子焼き、唐揚げ、鍋、雑炊、ひれ酒、家族経営、夜は飲み物込みで1人約50,000円。

cultural_comfort.note: Referral-only: a regular must introduce you; no first-time bookings.

tokyo_provision_roppongi.gf_detail: Ask. French-based à la carte with pasta, risotto, gratin and gyoza on the menu (2026 reviews); nothing is said about gluten.
tokyo_provision_roppongi.vegan_detail: Ask. The dishes described are meat, seafood and cheese; salad and sorbet also appear (January 2026). No vegan dishes are described.
tokyo_provision_roppongi.hours_raw: Tabelog: daily 18:00–24:00. The official site gives 18:00–2:00, with phone calls from 15:00; hours here follow Tabelog and are marked irregular. Members only: a "subscription restaurant" entered by fingerprint. The monthly fee covers almost all food and drink for the member and up to three guests, any number of visits: Unison ¥55,000 a month, De Luxe ¥88,000 a month incl. caviar, foie gras and truffle dishes (official site, tax included); some wines and premium items cost extra. Fees are charged monthly to a registered credit card, nothing is paid on the day; application through the official site. Drinks keep being refilled with the same drink unless you say otherwise (2026 reviews). 20 seats. Non-smoking. BYO drinks possible (Tabelog). Opened 18 February 2016 (Tabelog); a subscription restaurant since autumn 2017 (official site).
tokyo_provision_roppongi.notes: [French · Roppongi, a members-only subscription restaurant] A plain, unsigned third floor between Midtown and Roppongi crossing, opened by fingerprint: Provision has been a "subscription restaurant" since 2017, where a monthly fee — ¥55,000, or ¥88,000 to include caviar, foie gras and truffle dishes — covers nearly everything a member and up to three guests eat and drink, with no limit on visits. The cooking is French-based and seasonal: the house clams steamed in white wine, then risotto in the clam broth, ostrich with sea urchin, game in winter, and glasses that are refilled until you say stop. Guests of members in 2025–2026 enjoyed the concept and the food, though one found nothing mind-blowing. Members and invited guests only; apply on the official site.

chef_bio.background: Per the official site: opened in winter 2016 as "a restaurant that conveys the present", and relaunched in autumn 2017 as a subscription restaurant; featured on Fuji TV's "ポップUP！" (October 2022) and in LEON (March 2022 issue). An August 2026 reviewer also mentions the TV show "Matsuko & Ariyoshi Karisome Tengoku". An October 2025 diner found the master friendly and entertaining. No one is named in the sources read.
chef_bio.philosophy: Drop in any time, like a newspaper subscription, and enjoy wine and food with friends as often as you like (official site).
chef_bio.specialty: Clams steamed in white wine; clam-broth risotto.

anecdotes.text: "The entrance opens with a fingerprint authentication system, which adds an exciting touch." — December 2025.
"One standout dish was the restaurant's specialty, "Clams Steamed in White Wine."" — May 2026.
"As for drinks, … the same beverage is continuously poured unless you specify otherwise." — August 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイト (provision-tokyo.com): 六本木 大人のフレンチレストラン Provision、2016年冬に六本木交差点やミッドタウンからすぐの路地裏に開店、2017年秋にサブスクリプションレストランに。会員制の扉は指紋登録、月額会費のみでほぼすべての飲食: Unison (会員含め4名まで) 月55,000円、De Luxe (会員含め4名まで) 月88,000円 (キャビア、フォアグラ、トリュフも)、一部追加料金、クレジットカードで毎月自動決済、年会費一括も。営業18:00〜翌2:00、電話は15時から。港区六本木4-5-13 Reve六本木3F、六本木駅7番出口徒歩2分。食べログ: 毎日18:00〜24:00、20席、禁煙、持ち込み可、2016年2月18日オープン。口コミ(2025年10月〜2026年10月): 指紋認証の入口、白ワイン蒸しの蛤、蛤の出汁のリゾット、飲み物は言わないと同じものが注がれ続ける。

cultural_comfort.note: Members and invited guests only; entry by fingerprint.

existence.note: Shop-maintained (corporate-member) Tabelog listing and official site (© 2016–2026); reviews dated through October 2026.

tokyo_ramen_toyoki_ningyocho.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: wheat noodles in every bowl; gyoza alongside.
tokyo_ramen_toyoki_ningyocho.vegan_detail: Not vegan: pork-bone and Chinese-style soups, minced pork, chashu.
tokyo_ramen_toyoki_ningyocho.hours_raw: Tabelog lists only "open until 26:00"; opening time and closing days are not given. Diners report lunch from about 11:30 (customers already inside just before 11:30, August 2026) and late-night bowls at 23:00 (September 2026); a May 2026 diner gives the close as 1 AM. Cash or PayPay; no cards or e-money (Tabelog). 13 seats: counter inside plus one four-seat table outside, the only place smoking is allowed (Tabelog). No reservations. Opened 12 May 2016 (Tabelog).
tokyo_ramen_toyoki_ningyocho.notes: [Ramen · Ningyocho, the late-night bowl after drinks] A small ramen counter open until the small hours, where Ningyocho drinkers come to finish the night; at 23:00 on a September night it was more than half full, with many customers still drinking. The menu covers nearly every style. Tantanmen tops the list (¥1,080): sesame over a light soy-based soup, gently spicy and slightly tangy, with medium-thin curly noodles. Regulars swear by the tonkotsu shio, and one June diner found grated ginger lifting the tonkotsu shoyu. A couple runs the shop and the kitchen moves fast (October 2026); the owner, from China, is always smiling (October 2025). Prices have risen about 20% since opening (December 2025), and one diner found the noodle portion small. Cash or PayPay.

roles: Owner (unnamed; "The Chinese owner is always smiling and very quick", October 2025 review)
Run by a couple (October 2026 review)
chef_bio.background: Opened 12 May 2016 (Tabelog). A regular since opening says the owner's wife helps at busy times (December 2024); "The couple running the place work in perfect harmony" (October 2026).
chef_bio.specialty: Tantanmen; tonkotsu shio ramen.

anecdotes.text: "The couple running the place work in perfect harmony, and watching the efficient kitchen operation is quite pleasant." — October 2026, fourth visit.
"I visited around 11 PM. I thought it might be empty at this hour, but to my surprise, the restaurant was more than half full." — September 2026.
"Notably, the flavor of grated ginger infused in the broth adds a unique sharpness and character" — June 2026, tonkotsu shoyu.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ: らーめん豊樹、ラーメン、日本橋人形町3-3-13 CICビル 1F、人形町駅A5出口から徒歩2分、営業は26:00まで (開店時刻と定休日の記載なし)、カード・電子マネー不可、PayPay可、13席 (カウンターと外の4人席)、喫煙は外の席のみ、予約不可、2016年5月12日オープン。口コミ(2024年2月〜2026年10月): 醤油、塩、味噌、豚骨醤油、豚骨塩、担々麺、つけ麺、油そば、野菜らーめん、担々麺1,080円 (胡麻、辛さ控えめ、しびれなし、少し酸味、中細の縮れ麺)、汁なし担々麺、冷やし担々麺1,080円、豚骨醤油980円 (おろし生姜)、Aセット (半ライスと餃子3個) 250円、夫婦で営む、中国出身の店主、開店時より約2割値上げ、深夜も客が多い、麺が少なめという声も。

tokyo_okideli_horidome.gf_detail: Ask. Many cuts come with sauce or soy-sauce seasoning (the soy-sauce colon, 2025), alongside salt-seasoned tongue; noodles and Korean pancakes are on the menu. Nothing is described as gluten-free.
tokyo_okideli_horidome.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a beef yakiniku restaurant.
tokyo_okideli_horidome.hours_raw: Mon–Sat 17:00–23:00 (food last order 22:10, last entry 22:00); Sun and holidays 17:00–22:30 (last order 21:50, last entry 21:30); closing days irregular, posted monthly on Instagram (Tabelog). Reservations taken; booking calls after 16:00; parties of five or more confirm with the shop; reservations held 20 minutes; same-day cancellations may be charged; children not yet at school are not admitted (Tabelog). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners, UnionPay) and PayPay (Tabelog). 16 table seats; non-smoking, with a smoking area on the outside stairs (Tabelog). Full by 18:30 on a Saturday, with walk-ins waiting (February 2025).
tokyo_okideli_horidome.notes: [Yakiniku · Horidome-cho, a butcher-run wagyu grill with roots in the Oki Islands] A sixteen-seat yakiniku room on a second floor near Ningyocho, run by a butcher, whose chef comes from the Oki Islands off Shimane (Tabelog). The meat reportedly comes through a butcher in the Oki Islands (July 2026), and the rice is grown under contract there. Black wagyu is cut fresh and grilled over charcoal, staff explain each cut (June 2026), and a February 2026 meal began with kimchi, namul and Korean seaweed. The tongue, the outside skirt and the soy-sauce colon draw the most praise. Most diners praise the service and value, but one February 2025 diner found the meat no better than all-you-can-eat. Booking is wise: it fills by 18:30 on Saturdays. No preschool children.

roles: Chefs with a background in Japanese cuisine (Tabelog)
Run, it seems, by a couple (February 2025 review)
chef_bio.origin: The chef's hometown is Oki Island (Tabelog)
chef_bio.background: Per Tabelog: a butcher-run yakiniku; the chef's hometown is Oki Island, and the shop serves its ingredients, including contract-farmed "Oki Sea Salt Rice" milled just before shipping; the chefs have a background in Japanese cuisine; black wagyu from across the country through the shop's own sourcing routes. A July 2026 review says the meat comes from a butcher shop on an island in Shimane Prefecture.
chef_bio.specialty: Freshly cut black wagyu; house prosciutto of lean beef.

anecdotes.text: "It seems to be run by a butcher shop, and the staff kindly explained the different cuts of fresh meat, which we enjoyed immensely." — June 2026.
"The Colon is seasoned with soy sauce but isn’t overly salty; it has a rich flavor." — June 2025, a payday-weekend regular.
"The service and atmosphere were great, but the meat was simply not good." — February 2025.

tokyo_vigaro_nihonbashi_ningyocho.gf_detail: Ask. A European-style wagyu curry; nothing is described as gluten-free, and toppings include fried garlic.
tokyo_vigaro_nihonbashi_ningyocho.vegan_detail: Not vegan: wagyu curry with a black-wagyu consommé.
tokyo_vigaro_nihonbashi_ningyocho.hours_raw: Mon–Fri 11:30–16:00, open on weekday holidays, until the curry runs out; closed Saturday and Sunday (Tabelog). Pay first at order; water is self-service (Tabelog; 2026 reviews). Cards, transport IC, iD, QUICPay and QR (PayPay, Alipay, WeChat Pay and more) (Tabelog). 10 seats — one table for four and three for two (August 2026). Non-smoking. English menu; takeaway; Uber Eats (Tabelog). Opened 7 October 2025 (Tabelog). The owner works alone, so waits run long at lunch: 40 minutes to be seated and 20 more for the curry in December 2025, about 50 minutes in September 2026, about 15 minutes in October 2026.
tokyo_vigaro_nihonbashi_ningyocho.notes: [Curry · Ningyocho, a one-person wagyu curry counter up a hidden staircase] A ten-seat curry shop on a second floor reached by a steep staircase behind a red sign, opened in October 2025 and run single-handed by a young owner. There is one curry, a European-style wagyu curry blanketed in spices, rich and slightly sweet, for ¥800, plus a long list of toppings and a free, very hot black-wagyu consommé. The recipe keeps evolving: one regular has tracked three versions in its first year. Diners love the owner's warmth and the value, but everything is cooked by one person, so lunch waits can stretch from 15 minutes to nearly an hour. Come at the 11:30 opening if you are in a hurry. Weekdays only, until the curry runs out.

roles: Owner, working alone ("The young owner manages everything alone", August 2026 review)

A diner cites the shop's Instagram for domestic A5 wagyu (August 2026). Menu changes are announced on Instagram (Tabelog).
chef_bio.specialty: Premium Wagyu Golden Curry.

"Initially, the menu featured the Ultimate European Curry (JPY 1200 …), which used A5 grade domestic black wagyu beef" — August 2026, ninth visit.

tokyo_au_pas_camarade_ningyocho.gf_detail: Ask when booking — the shop asks for allergies with dinner reservations (Tabelog). Lunch includes yakisoba and a sweet gravy over the wagyu rice; nothing is described as gluten-free.
tokyo_au_pas_camarade_ningyocho.vegan_detail: Not vegan: wagyu-centred teppanyaki and beef soups; the seasonal steamed vegetables come within a meat set.
tokyo_au_pas_camarade_ningyocho.hours_raw: Mon 17:00–22:00 (last order 20:30); Tue–Sat 11:30–14:00 (last order 13:30) and 17:00–22:00 (last order 20:30); closed Sundays and holidays (Tabelog). Reservations for dinner only; tell the shop about allergies and dislikes when booking (Tabelog). Tabelog lists cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners), but a July 2026 lunch diner was told cash only. Service charge 10% (Tabelog). 11 seats: 7 at a counter around the teppan and a sunken-kotatsu private room for 4–5; private rooms for 2, 4 or 6; private hire up to 20 (Tabelog). Non-smoking. Lunch is cooked to order by two staff, so waits of about 20 minutes (April, July 2026). Opened 18 May 2019 (Tabelog).
tokyo_au_pas_camarade_ningyocho.notes: [Teppanyaki · Ningyocho, Japanese-French teppan in a back alley, with a celebrated wagyu lunch] A small teppanyaki restaurant in a Ningyocho back alley, since 2019, cooking Japanese-French omakase at a seven-seat counter around the griddle, with tatami private rooms. Dinner is a course of small plates ending in wagyu and rice, with wines picked daily by a sommelier. Lunch is the bargain that built its reputation: black-wagyu steamed rice for ¥2,000, the meat almost rare and finishing in the heat of the rice, or a yakisoba in squid-liver sauce for ¥1,200. Two people cook lunch to order, so expect about 20 minutes. One July 2026 diner was told lunch is cash only, though Tabelog lists cards. A sister restaurant in Ginza is mentioned (July 2026).

chef_bio.background: Opened 18 May 2019 (Tabelog). The interior has been renovated, with spacious counter seating (June 2026). "It seems there is a sister restaurant in Ginza as well" (July 2026 review).
chef_bio.philosophy: Creative dishes combining Japanese and French cuisine with meat, seafood and vegetables from across Japan, in small portions (Tabelog shop text).
chef_bio.specialty: Wagyu steamed rice; teppan yakisoba with squid-liver sauce.

anecdotes.text: "As I ate, the heat from the rice gradually cooked the meat, making it even more flavorful with the melted fat." — July 2026, black-wagyu steamed rice.
"… during lunch, … just two staff members, so cooking starts after the order is placed." — April 2026.
"The sauce, which highlights the umami of the squid innards, was impressive and offered a unique take on yakisoba" — April 2026, ¥1,200.

tokyo_khana_khaja_okachimachi.gf_detail: GF — ask: no gluten-free statement. Curry with rice avoids the wheat naan, but the curries, the Manchurian dishes and the fried pakora are not described as wheat-free.
tokyo_khana_khaja_okachimachi.vegan_detail: Some vegan options: the restaurant's own Tabelog text says it caters to vegan diners and lists vegetarian options; the menu has many vegetable and bean curries (mixed vegetable, dal tadka, chana masala, aloo gobi, bhindi masala) and vegetable biryani. Which are vegan is not marked — several use butter, cream or paneer — so ask.
tokyo_khana_khaja_okachimachi.hours_raw: Daily 11:00–23:00: lunch 11:00–16:00, dinner 16:00–23:00 (last order 22:30); open all year (Tabelog). Reservations taken; Tabelog points can be used (September 2026). 26 seats (one table for four, seven for two); private hire up to 20. Non-smoking. Payment: Tabelog lists cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners, UnionPay) and e-money, no QR; a February 2026 review said cash only at lunch and dinner. Free Wi-Fi. Take-out and delivery within 1 km. Kids' menu; strollers can be stored.
tokyo_khana_khaja_okachimachi.notes: [Indian-Nepali curry · Okachimachi, a basement curry house open 11 to 11] A basement Indian and Nepali restaurant a minute from Okachimachi Station, open every day from 11:00 to 23:00. Lunch runs until 16:00, which makes it a handy late lunch: curry with freshly baked naan or rice, salad and a drink from ¥900, with one free refill of naan or rice; the cheese-naan set (¥1,350) and the Ladies' Set (¥1,200 in 2026) are the reviewers' favourites. The curries are mild unless you ask — even 'super hot' did not feel very spicy to a June 2026 diner. At night there are tandoori grills, biryani and Nepali beer. The restaurant says it caters to halal and vegan diners; vegetable and bean curries are plentiful, but ask which are made without butter or cream. Staff speak English and the menu is in English.

chef_bio.origin: Per the listing, open nearly 10 years with a Nepali chef cooking the same recipes since opening (Tabelog official text)
chef_bio.background: Tabelog official listing; per the listing, the butter chicken uses a spice blend made from scratch and naan is baked to order in a tandoor. No source names the chef.
chef_bio.specialty: Butter chicken curry; cheese naan.

anecdotes.text: "The Butter Chicken was excellent, but the Spinach Curry was among the top two or three I've ever tried" — May 2026, cheese naan set.
"I chose super hot, but it wasn't that spicy." — June 2026, chicken curry lunch ¥950.

tokyo_hasi_bero_higashiueno.vegan_detail: Vegan — ask: mostly meat, fish and cheese plates; baba ganoush and the homemade pickles may suit, but nothing is marked vegan.
tokyo_hasi_bero_higashiueno.hours_raw: Mon, Tue, Wed, Fri 11:30–14:00 and 17:00–23:30; Sat, Sun and holidays 15:00–23:30; last orders food 23:00, drinks 23:15; closed Thursdays (Tabelog). Reservations taken; a reviewer booked for a later day when it was full (October 2026). 9 counter seats, plus standing tables (up to 15 standing). No drink menu — staff recommend natural wines by the glass (February and October 2026). Non-smoking. Cards, transport IC and QR payments. Children welcome. Opened 13 September 2024.
tokyo_hasi_bero_higashiueno.notes: [Wine bar · Naka-Okachimachi, natural wine under the clock tower] A small natural-wine bistro bar in a striking building with a clock tower in Higashi-Ueno, opened in September 2024 by sommeliers and chefs from the Blue Note group. Inside is a nine-seat counter, standing tables, a DJ booth and a nostalgic Showa-era feel. There is no drink list: tell the staff what you like and a glass is chosen for you. The food is better than a bar needs — fig butter, mushroom carpaccio, assorted appetizers, pasta of the day, a creamy massaman curry, New Orleans gumbo — and lunch plates run ¥1,150–1,500. Most reviewers in 2026 found the owner friendly and the place relaxing; one in February 2026 found the service lacking and left after one drink. Weekends get busy; weekdays are said to be quieter (October 2026).

chef_bio.background: Per the Tabelog listing (official information), run by sommeliers and chefs who trained in the Blue Note group. Reviewers in June and August 2026 describe a friendly owner who picks the wines. No source names the owner or chefs.
chef_bio.philosophy: Per the listing: dishes that mix French cooking with flavours from many countries, paired with natural wine and music, with DJ events.
chef_bio.specialty: Natural wine; gumbo; curry.

anecdotes.text: "The owner recommended a Tempranillo from Sept Winery in Lebanon, which pairs perfectly with the brown mushroom carpaccio and fig butter!" — June 2026.
"Inside, there's a DJ booth and carefully selected speakers, creating a nostalgic and relaxing space." — June 2026.

tokyo_bai_en_inaricho.gf_detail: GF — ask: no gluten-free statement. The signature yodare-dori sauce uses soy sauce (owner-chef, 2023), and lunches include wonton noodles and dumplings; dinner is a set course, so ask when booking.
tokyo_bai_en_inaricho.vegan_detail: Not vegan: the medicinal soups are built on chicken and pork stock (2023) or dried scallop (October 2026), and the courses centre on chicken, foie gras, seafood, shark fin and beef.
tokyo_bai_en_inaricho.hours_raw: Lunch 11:30–15:00 (last order 14:00) and dinner 18:00–20:00 (last order 19:00), Tue–Sun and holidays; closed Mondays (Savor Japan / Hitosara listing — undated, carries an old shortened-hours notice). Tabelog lists no hours and says closing days are not fixed — confirm when booking. 2026 reviews found lunch open at 11:30 on a weekday, a Sunday and holidays. Dinner is a set course only and needs a booking (owner-chef, 2023); the dinner course can also be booked for lunch. Lunch can queue (about 10 people in the rain, September 2026); bookings get in first. Service charge 10%. 23 seats (12 sofa, 6 in private rooms, 4 at the counter). Non-smoking. Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners); no e-money or QR. BYO allowed (Tabelog). Opened 8 September 2019.
tokyo_bai_en_inaricho.notes: [Chinese · Inaricho, medicinal soups and a foie-gras 'candy apple'] A small second-floor Chinese restaurant a minute from Inaricho Station, easy to miss behind a small sign on an outside staircase. Owner-chef 白岩勝也 trained in Beijing, Hong Kong and Taiwan and cooks 'ikkyosai' — dishes meant to evoke a scene — with no chemical seasonings and a medicinal soup that changes with the 24 seasonal terms, never repeated since opening in 2019 (san-tatsu, 2023). Dinner is a booked set course (about ¥10,000–15,000) that opens with a cherry-sized 'candy apple' of tea-smoked foie gras in hibiscus jelly. Lunch is the way in: tender yodare-dori in two house chilli oils for ¥1,400 on weekdays, or a ¥2,500 set with the medicinal soup, with a bottomless sour-plum drink. It made Tabelog's Chinese TOKYO 100 in 2024 and 2026, and cooked lunch on the TRAIN SUITE Shikishima (September 2026 review). Lunch can queue, especially on holidays.

roles: owner-chef
chef_bio.background: Owner-chef; trained in Beijing, Hong Kong, Taiwan and elsewhere in China (san-tatsu, June 2023). Chose a small space "where I can see the guests' faces"; the hideaway feel was not planned (san-tatsu, 2023).
chef_bio.philosophy: Food-as-medicine (医食同源) Chinese cooking from natural ingredients with no chemical seasonings; medicinal soups changed to match the 24 seasonal terms (san-tatsu, 2023).
chef_bio.specialty: Yodare-dori; medicinal soup; foie-gras "candy apple".

tokyo_saruyama_kitchen_ueno_zoo.hours_raw: Daily 10:00–16:30; closed on days Ueno Zoo is closed (Tabelog: "follows Ueno Zoo's schedule"). Inside Ueno Zoo's East Garden. No reservations. Busy from about 11:00–12:30; easier after 12:30 or mid-afternoon (2026 reviews). 180 seats (60 on 1F, 120 on 2F); terrace. Non-smoking. Cards (VISA, JCB), transport IC, QUICPay and QR payments. No service charge. Wheelchair accessible; baby-changing, nursing room; strollers welcome (some seats lack stroller space, August 2026); kids' menu. Take-out. Opened 26 February 2020.
tokyo_saruyama_kitchen_ueno_zoo.notes: [Cafeteria · Ueno Zoo, the zoo food court by the monkey mountain] A food court in Ueno Zoo's East Garden: a clean, two-floor cafeteria with 180 seats, panda illustrations and a terrace, open 10:00–16:30 on zoo days. Order rice bowls such as glossy grilled pork belly or thick pork-tenderloin katsu (large +¥100), meat udon, a summer chilled tomato tantanmen (¥1,000), and fries; children get an udon set topped with panda-shaped fish cake. Seasonal novelties are the fun part — a matcha shaved ice with a monkey-shaped wafer, otter-shaped meat buns, and an elephant soda each August for Arun, the zoo's Asian elephant. Reviewers in 2026 found it fairly priced and tasty, though some said the portions, even large, are small. Lines peak 11:00–12:30; go earlier or after.

chef_bio.background: Cafeteria inside Ueno Zoo (East Garden); Tabelog lists the zoo's restaurant page as its website. No source names the operator.
chef_bio.specialty: Rice bowls; animal-themed snacks.

tokyo_tadano_yakitori_yotsuya.gf_detail: Ask. The skewers come in a set course and include miso-marinated thigh; the finishes are soboro rice with a ginger-soy seasoning or grilled rice balls in chicken broth. Nothing gluten-free is described.
tokyo_tadano_yakitori_yotsuya.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a chicken house; the courses are skewers, chicken broth and minced-chicken rice.
tokyo_tadano_yakitori_yotsuya.hours_raw: Mon–Sat 17:30–22:00; closed Sunday, holidays and every other Saturday; hours may change (Tabelog). Reservations taken. Courses only, plus a few chicken dishes à la carte (April 2023). 20 seats: a counter, a table for two and one for four; whole-shop hire possible; smoking allowed (Tabelog; April 2023). Cards (JCB, AMEX, Diners); no e-money or QR (Tabelog). Spend about ¥6,000–10,000 a head with sake (2025–26 reviews).
tokyo_tadano_yakitori_yotsuya.notes: [Yakitori · Yotsuya, a long-running charcoal counter in a back lane] A small, homely yakitori shop at the back of a building one street behind Shinjuku-dōri, run for decades — a January 2025 regular of more than 20 years says it opened 36 years ago — by a master whom diners praise for both the grilling and the welcome. Everything comes as a course of six or ten skewers, each served the moment it leaves the charcoal, from wasabi chicken breast and liver to the soft-boiled quail egg diners rave about; finish with soboro rice or grilled rice balls in chicken broth. Pick your sake from the one-sho bottles in the fridge by the door. Cramped but friendly: the closeness makes it easy to talk to other guests (May 2024), and a solo guest drank at the counter in September 2026. Closed Sundays and alternate Saturdays; smoking is allowed.

tokyo_tonkatsu_yakitori_an_yotsuya.hours_raw: Daily 11:30–15:00 (last order 14:30) and 17:00–23:00 (last order 22:00); New Year hours on the website (Tabelog). Frying takes time: a Sunday lunch cutlet took nearly 20 minutes (August 2026). 51 seats with counter, sofas and private rooms for up to 14; hire up to 42 seated or 70 standing; non-smoking, smoking at a nearby facility (Tabelog). Cards, e-money and QR including PayPay, Alipay and WeChat Pay (Tabelog). English menu and English-speaking staff; wheelchair accessible (Tabelog).
tokyo_tonkatsu_yakitori_an_yotsuya.notes: [Tonkatsu · Yotsuya, a hotel-basement cutlet and yakitori room] In the basement of Hotel Keihan Tokyo Yotsuya, a stylish, high-ceilinged room with an Italian-looking counter that surprises people expecting a cutlet shop. A sign says it revives the tonkatsu of the former Akasaka Fritz, and one diner names the supervising chef as Motoshiro Saito. Lunch is a loin cutlet set from ¥1,500 with free large rice; dinner is courses for groups, built around a pork shabu-shabu cooked in soba broth with unlimited ribbon-sliced daikon and soba to finish. Opinions on the cutlet split: one regular finds it far better than a nearby specialist and another found it pink and juicy inside, while October 2026 diners found it ordinary, unevenly fried, or small and lukewarm, and one called the Fritz claim misleading. Friendly service, English menu, open every day.

chef_bio.background: No source names the cooks. October 2026 reviews: a sign says "the famous tonkatsu restaurant 'Akasaka Fritz,' which used to be at the Nagatacho Prudential Hotel, has reopened"; another diner writes it offers fried foods "under the supervision of Mr. Motoshiro Saito, who aimed to recreate the flavors of the former Fritz in Akasaka" and found the result fell short. A September 2026 diner calls Fritz "the predecessor of Pochi-ken". Tabelog: "Enjoy exquisite fritz tonkatsu, expertly grilled skewers, and a selection of sake and shochu from across the country"; private rooms and hire for up to 70 standing. A search shows another "とんかつ & 焼鳥 An" in Akasaka-mitsuke (一休 listing title; page not opened).

tokyo_yotsuya_haraku_chi.gf_detail: Ask. Fried mehikari and Date chicken kara-age, gyoza and soba are wheat-based, and the horse sashimi comes with miso; nothing gluten-free is described.
tokyo_yotsuya_haraku_chi.vegan_detail: Ask. Edamame with salt koji appears, but the menu centres on fish, Date chicken and horse, and the appetizer one September 2026 diner received was anglerfish soup.
tokyo_yotsuya_haraku_chi.hours_raw: Mon–Sat 18:00 to 22:00 last order; closing days not fixed (Tabelog). Reservations recommended on weekdays, which get busy (2024–25 reviews); some dishes sell out (September 2026). 20 seats with a counter; non-smoking; whole-shop hire up to 20; children welcome (Tabelog). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX), Suica, iD and PayPay (Tabelog). In a residential lane, about 7 minutes from Yotsuya Station per Tabelog.
tokyo_yotsuya_haraku_chi.notes: [Izakaya · Yotsuya, a taste of Fukushima in a back lane] A clean, beige 20-seat izakaya hidden in a residential lane behind Yotsuya Station, run by an owner from Date in Fukushima; the name, one diner explains, is Fukushima dialect for a full stomach. The menu is Fukushima's: crisp fried mehikari you eat bones and all, ika-ninjin of squid and carrot, Fukushima gyoza, tender Date chicken as steak, kara-age or prosciutto, horse sashimi with spicy miso, and to finish, soba in a Date chicken meatball soup. A long list of Fukushima sake comes with tasting notes and a choice of cups. People from Fukushima gather here and chat with the owner. Not everyone felt welcome: a February 2025 diner who arrived an hour before closing got a cold reception, found the sake overpriced and an item left on the table unsanitary. Book ahead on weekdays.

chef_bio.origin: The owner is from Date City, Fukushima ("The owner hails from Date City, Fukushima", March 2024).
chef_bio.background: No source names the owner. "There were people from Fukushima in the restaurant who had friendly conversations with the owner" (January 2024); "This restaurant is run by someone from Fukushima" (February 2025); "The name 'Haraku-chi' means 'full stomach' in the Fukushima dialect" (September 2026).
chef_bio.specialty: Fried mehikari; Date chicken; Fukushima sake.

"First, I was amazed by the appetizer: anglerfish soup!" — September 2026, brought by locals from Fukushima.
"I received a cold reception, possibly because I arrived an hour before closing." — February 2025.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ: 四ッ谷haraku-chi、居酒屋、四谷1-11 BELL ALLEY 1F、四ツ谷駅から徒歩7分、月〜土18:00〜22:00 (L.O.)、不定休、20席、禁煙、貸切20名まで、子ども可、カード・電子マネー・PayPay 可。口コミ(2024年1月〜2026年9月): Fukushima の料理と日本酒、店主は Date 市の出身、店名はFukushima の方言で満腹の意味という声、めひかりのkara-age、いかにんじん、Fukushima の gyoza、Date 鶏のチキンステーキ、馬刺しと辛味噌、あんこうの汁、締めは Date 鶏のつくねのつけ汁のそば、選べるお猪口、平日は混む、2025年2月には冷たい対応だったという声。

tokyo_sushi_mitani_yotsuya.gf_detail: Ask through the person who books: the omakase uses soy-based seasonings (e.g. dashi soy sauce with the uni) and includes fried dishes (fried kuro-mutsu, fried abalone, hairy crab croquette); nothing gluten-free is described.
tokyo_sushi_mitani_yotsuya.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a fish and shellfish omakase with dashi and caviar.
tokyo_sushi_mitani_yotsuya.hours_raw: Wed–Sun 18:00–22:30 (last order 22:00); closed Monday and Tuesday; no lunch (Tabelog). Booking: reservation only and no new reservations accepted (Tabelog); diners get in through regulars' invitations or rebook a year or two ahead (2024–26 reviews). 6 counter seats, all starting together; whole-counter hire for up to 6 (Tabelog; July 2026). Spend about ¥60,000–100,000+ per head with the pairing; one guest who switched the pairing to champagne paid ¥300,000 (September 2026). Non-alcoholic tea pairing on request (July 2026). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners); no e-money or QR (Tabelog).
tokyo_sushi_mitani_yotsuya.notes: [Sushi · Yotsuya, the six-seat counter with no new bookings] Tabelog Gold seven times (2019–2024 and 2026), a six-seat wooden counter a few minutes from Yotsuya Station where chef Mitani serves an omakase that diners describe as a pairing performance as much as a sushi meal: each appetizer and every few pieces of nigiri arrive with a drink chosen for them, from Burgundy and old champagne to rare sake or cold-brewed Yame tea, and the rice is reseasoned for each topping. Ingredients are named by their fisherman or maker, such as Awaji sea bream, Yoichi uni, Nakatsugawa caviar and Ariake nori, and the course runs to about 25 servings ending in anago. Diners praise the chef's warm smile and the hospitality of the floor staff. It takes no new reservations: seats go to regulars, who often rebook a year or two ahead, and their guests. Expect ¥60,000 to well over ¥100,000 a head.

roles: Chef (reviews: "the chef, Mr. Mitani"; "I greeted the lively chef Mitani")
chef_bio.background: Tabelog: Mitani (三谷, ミタニ); Tabelog Award Silver 2017, 2018 and 2025, Gold 2019–2024 and 2026; Sushi TOKYO "Tabelog 100" 2021, 2022, 2025; reservation only, no new reservations. Reviews: "The chef, who tells a story of gratitude through sushi after overcoming various challenges, along with the floor staff, provides remarkable hospitality" (July 2026); "The chef's warm smile… was also fantastic" (October 2026). No source gives the chef's given name or the kanji of the chef's name.
chef_bio.specialty: Sushi with drink pairings; anago to finish.

anecdotes.text: "After a two-year wait, I finally had the chance to visit again… We enjoyed my favorite, Chateau d'Yquem, and concluded with a final course of 20 pieces of anago (sea eel) served with two types: salt and sweet sauce." — September 2026.
"On this day, I requested a non-alcoholic pairing and enjoyed three types of cold-brewed Yame tea." — July 2026.
"Since I can't drink those, they kindly switched everything to champagne for me. The cost was JPY 300,000 per person." — September 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ: 三谷 (ミタニ)、寿司、四谷1-22-1、JR四ツ谷駅から徒歩4分、丸ノ内線・南北線5分、水〜日18:00〜22:30 (L.O.22:00)、月火休み、昼の営業なし、完全予約制、新規の予約は受け付けていない、6席 (カウンターのみ)、貸切6名まで、禁煙、カード可、食べログアワード Silver 2017・2018・2025、Gold 2019〜2024・2026、寿司 TOKYO 百名店2021・2022・2025。口コミ(2024年11月〜2026年10月): 一品ごとのワインや日本酒のペアリング、Yame の水出し茶のノンアルコールのペアリング、Yoichi のうに、Awaji の真鯛、Nakatsugawa のキャビア、締めの穴子、予約は1〜2年待ち、1人6万〜10万円以上。

tokyo_shirato_roppongi.gf_detail: Ask. An omakase of small dishes that has included house focaccia, a fried dish with tartar sauce and a truffle ramen (July–August 2026); nothing is said about gluten.
tokyo_shirato_roppongi.vegan_detail: Ask. Tabelog lists vegetarian options, but the courses are built on fish, shellfish and meat and no vegan course is described.
tokyo_shirato_roppongi.hours_raw: Tue–Fri 18:00–23:00 (last order 22:30); Sat, Sun and holidays also lunch 11:30–15:00 (last order 13:00); closed Mondays (Tabelog). All guests are served at the same time, so please be punctual. 10% service charge. 8 counter seats; private hire up to 20. Non-smoking. Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX); no e-money. English menu. BYO possible. Alcoholic and non-alcoholic pairings cost extra. Opened 21 October 2019 (Tabelog).
tokyo_shirato_roppongi.notes: [French · Roppongi, a white 8-seat counter of 20 small seasonal dishes] Up on the second floor a minute from Roppongi Station, an L-shaped counter of eight before an open kitchen, in a room of white plaster, wood, earth and stone — the name means "white soil". Chef Seiji Shirato cooks about twenty small plates of seasonal produce from around Japan, French at heart but borrowing from Japanese and Chinese cooking: brandy-marinated botan shrimp, charcoal-grilled nodoguro with soup de poisson, Ezo venison with two-year-aged potatoes, even a truffle ramen. Diners in 2026 loved the variety and the drink or tea pairings; one found the sauces a touch sweet. Dinner ¥24,200; weekend lunch ¥9,900.

chef_bio.chef_name: Seiji Shirato (as written in the Tabelog shop text)
roles: Chef (Tabelog shop text)
chef_bio.background: Per the Tabelog shop text: chef Seiji Shirato trained at a hotel in Tokyo, spent three years as sous chef at a bistro in Azabu-Juban, and opened this restaurant at 29. A July 2026 diner describes the chef running the place solo; an August 2026 diner saw one chef cooking and a staff member serving drinks. Opened 21 October 2019 (Tabelog).
chef_bio.philosophy: Each ingredient cooked in the way that tastes best, whether Japanese, Western or Chinese (Tabelog shop text).
chef_bio.specialty: Nodoguro soup de poisson; about 20 small seasonal dishes.

anecdotes.text: "One standout dish was the "Botan Ebi (Sweet Shrimp) marinated in Brandy."" — May 2026, omakase course.
"This course, centered around fish dishes, kept me engaged until the end with various cooking methods such as grilling, frying, charcoal cooking, confit, and escabeche." — July 2026, ¥24,200 course.
"However, I found that the sauces for all the dishes were a bit on the sweet side." — September 2026, lunch ¥9,900.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ: 白土、港区六本木4-4-8 エトワール六本木ビル2F、六本木駅7番出口から徒歩1分、火〜金18:00〜23:00 (L.O.22:30)、土日祝は11:30〜15:00も、月休み、一斉スタート、サービス料10%、8席 (カウンター)、貸切20名まで、禁煙、カード可、英語メニュー、持ち込み可、ベジタリアンメニューあり、2019年10月21日オープン。店の紹介: 全国の旬の食材を和洋中にとらわれず約20品の小皿で、名物「のどぐろのスープ・ド・ポワソン」、ワイン・日本酒や国産茶のペアリング、白い漆喰の壁と土色のカウンター、シェフ Seiji Shirato (東京のホテル、Azabu-Juban のビストロで3年スーシェフ、29歳で独立)。コース24,200円、アルコールペアリング付き40,700円。口コミ(2026年1月〜9月): 昼のコース9,900円、ブランデー漬けの牡丹海老、炭火ののどぐろ、Ezo の鹿、Obanazawa の牛、トリュフのラーメン、ソースが少し甘いという声。

cultural_comfort.note: English menu (Tabelog); omakase at the counter.

tokyo_tempura_mikaku_roppongi.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: wheat-batter tempura, with a sweet-savoury tendon sauce.
tokyo_tempura_mikaku_roppongi.vegan_detail: Not vegan: the vegetable tendon includes an egg (January 2025 visit), and bowls come with tendon sauce and miso soup; most tempura is shrimp and fish.
tokyo_tempura_mikaku_roppongi.hours_raw: TEMPORARILY CLOSED for renovation since 1 September; the shop first aimed to reopen in mid-October and now plans early December (Tabelog notice). Before the closure: Mon–Fri and days before/after holidays, lunch 11:30–14:00 (last order 13:30) and dinner 18:00–22:00 (food last order 20:30, drinks 21:00); closed Saturdays, Sundays and holidays; dinner reservations until 15:00 the day before (Tabelog). Lunch queues at noon (June 2026). 30 seats: 9 at the counter, 8 at tables, 8 in a tatami room, 6 in a small room; private hire up to 20. Non-smoking inside. Cards, e-money and QR (PayPay, Alipay, WeChat Pay and others). Children and babies welcome. BYO, takeout and delivery.
tokyo_tempura_mikaku_roppongi.notes: [Tempura · Roppongi, a Showa-era tendon counter, closed for renovation until December] A long-established tempura house in a side street below Roppongi crossing — founded in Nihonbashi in 1931 and in Roppongi for about 30 years, per a June 2026 diner — with a counter, tables and a tatami room. Lunch is the famous part: tendon from ¥1,300, the salt tendon sprinkled with rock salt, and the ¥1,800 omakase bowl piled with shrimp, kisu, anago and a soft-boiled egg, fried in sesame and cottonseed oil, with a noon queue. Evenings bring tempura courses and a duck hot pot. Diners in 2026 found it great value for Roppongi; one found the salt bowl too salty. Closed for renovation since 1 September; reopening planned for early December.

chef_bio.origin: Founded in Nihonbashi in 1931; in Roppongi for about 30 years (June 2026 review)
chef_bio.background: A June 2026 diner writes that the shop was founded in Nihonbashi in 1931 and moved to Roppongi about 30 years ago; another June 2026 diner counted five staff at lunch, led by an owner who looked to be in the seventies age range; an August 2026 diner saw an elderly chef frying alone. No one is named in the sources read.
chef_bio.specialty: Tendon — sauce, salt and omakase.

anecdotes.text: "Upon my return, I can confidently say that this is the go-to place for tempura rice bowls in Roppongi." — June 2026, omakase tendon ¥1,800.
"Using Imai's first-pressed sesame oil and cottonseed oil, the tempura is remarkably flavorful and light." — June 2026.
"The salt tempura rice bowl, not dipped in sauce, is a serious challenge seasoned only with salt!" — August 2026, ¥1,500.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ (店舗会員): てんぷら 味覚、港区六本木6-7-17、六本木駅3番出口から徒歩3分、月〜金と祝前日・祝後日の11:30〜14:00 (L.O.13:30)、18:00〜22:00 (料理L.O.20:30)、土日祝休み、夜の予約は前日15時まで、30席 (カウンター9、テーブル8、座敷8、小部屋6)、貸切20名まで、店内禁煙、カード・電子マネー・QR可、子ども可、持ち込み・テイクアウト・デリバリー、ベジタリアンメニューあり。お知らせ: 9月1日から改装のため休業、10月中旬の再開予定が遅れ、12月上旬の再開をめざす。口コミ(2025年1月〜2026年8月): 1931年に Nihonbashi で創業、約30年前に六本木へ、天丼1,300円、塩天丼1,500円、おまかせ丼1,800円、ごま油と綿実油、夜のコースと鴨鍋、昼は行列。

tokyo_imoarai_zaka_no_shita_roppongi.gf_detail: Ask. The sukiyaki is simmered in a sweet-savoury sauce whose ingredients are not given, and the menu has breaded wagyu katsu, menchi katsu and tempura; nothing is called gluten-free.
tokyo_imoarai_zaka_no_shita_roppongi.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a wagyu kappo — beef sukiyaki and shabu-shabu with egg, Kyoto pork, chicken and fish dishes.
tokyo_imoarai_zaka_no_shita_roppongi.hours_raw: Daily 11:30–15:00 (last order 14:30) and 17:00–23:00 (food last order 22:00, drinks 22:30) (Tabelog). Lunch: walk-in on Wednesdays, Fridays and Saturdays; reservation needed on Mondays, Tuesdays, Thursdays and Sundays (Tabelog). Closed 29 November for a special holiday. ¥500 (plus tax) cover per person; one drink per person at dinner. 14 seats: 8 at the counter, 6 in semi-private rooms (private rooms for 4 or 6). Heated tobacco only, in a designated area. Cards, e-money and QR (PayPay, Alipay, WeChat Pay and others). Multilingual menu, many overseas guests (July 2026). Children welcome. Opened in 2025 (July 2026 review).
tokyo_imoarai_zaka_no_shita_roppongi.notes: [Sukiyaki · Roppongi, A5 Yamagata-beef sukiyaki for one at the foot of Imoarai-zaka] A retro-modern second-floor counter with semi-private rooms, opened in 2025, that makes wagyu sukiyaki casual: the "choi-suki" is two or three slices of A5 Yamagata strip loin simmered in a small iron pot in front of you and dipped not in raw egg but in a fluffy meringue of eggs offered at Ise Jingu — ¥4,480 as a set with vegetables and rice. Around it, a menu of drinking dishes from ¥500: beef-toro potato salad, Tokachi beef yukhoe, wagyu rare katsu. Diners in 2026 praised the meat, the cheerful manager and the value for Roppongi; many guests are from overseas. Course ¥9,900; ¥500 cover.

chef_bio.background: A July 2026 diner says the restaurant opened the previous year and found the manager and staff cheerful and chatty across the counter. A September 2026 diner notes Yamagata beef, Kyoto pork and vegetables from contracted farms. No one is named in the sources read.
chef_bio.philosophy: Wagyu dishes that go with a drink, and sukiyaki in small portions for a relaxed, casual evening (Tabelog shop text).
chef_bio.specialty: Choi-suki — single-portion A5 Yamagata sukiyaki with meringue egg.

anecdotes.text: "… a new style of sukiyaki called "Choi Suki," allowing you to order as few as 2 to 3 slices, making it perfect for enjoying as a snack or a main dish." — July 2026.
"The meat was, of course, delicious, but the meringue-like egg was a new experience for me." — September 2026, course with all-you-can-drink.
"It’s popular among inbound customers, with a multilingual menu available, making it easy to recommend to travelers from abroad." — July 2026.

tokyo_ichi_oku_roppongi.gf_detail: Ask. The tofu steak comes with a steak sauce, and the menu includes gyoza, spring rolls and katsu (2025–2026 reviews); nothing is said about gluten.
tokyo_ichi_oku_roppongi.vegan_detail: Ask. Tabelog lists vegetarian options, but the tofu steak is seasoned with dashi (March 2026) and most signatures are tuna, pork, oysters or shirasu.
tokyo_ichi_oku_roppongi.hours_raw: Mon–Sat 17:00–23:00 (food last order 22:00, drinks 22:30); closed Sundays and holidays; closed 16–19 August 2026 (Tabelog). Lunch, served for 35 years, ended on 20 December 2024 (Tabelog notice). ¥550 per person table charge at dinner. Dinner bills of ¥12,000 or less must be paid in cash; above that, cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners); no e-money or QR (Tabelog). 30 table seats; private hire for up to 50. Non-smoking inside, ashtray at the front. Children and strollers welcome (large strollers left outside). No printed menu: the menu is on the tables and you write your own order (2025–2026 reviews). Often full; booking recommended.
tokyo_ichi_oku_roppongi.notes: [Home cooking · Roppongi, a 1968 back-alley original known for its tofu steak] A warm, eclectic dining room in a quiet alley behind Midtown that has been feeding Roppongi since 1968 — the name, "one hundred million", came from the founder's hopes for Japan's population, its guests and its sales, as one reviewer tells it. There is no printed menu: dishes are listed on the tables and you write your own order, choosing among Japanese, Italian, Asian and Chinese plates that regulars return for — the crisp dashi tofu steak, ginger-grilled tuna, cheese-topped gyoza, Polynesian pork, oyster rice and a Showa pudding. Diners in 2025–2026 found it welcoming and often full. Dinner only; small bills are cash.

chef_bio.background: Founded in 1968 (Tabelog shop text; 2026 review). An August 2025 reviewer explains the name — Japan's population of one hundred million at the founding, the hope of one hundred million guests and of one hundred million yen in sales. A July 2025 diner saw the master practising qigong outside; a February 2026 diner praises the owner's warm hospitality and the posters by Tadanori Yokoo on the walls. No one is named in the sources read.
chef_bio.philosophy: A timeless place in a Roppongi back alley, with Japanese-inspired international cooking found nowhere else (Tabelog shop text).
chef_bio.specialty: Original tofu steak; ginger-grilled tuna.

anecdotes.text: "There is no printed menu; the tables themselves serve as the menu." — March 2026.
"I particularly enjoyed the stir-fried mushrooms, which are said to be simmered for 30 hours." — July 2025.
"The Aoyasa Shirasu, Ginger Grilled Tuna, and Teppan-yaki are must-orders!!" — November 2025.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ (店舗会員): 一億、港区六本木4-4-5、六本木駅から徒歩2分、Nogizaka 駅から5分、月〜土17:00〜23:00 (料理L.O.22:00、ドリンクL.O.22:30)、日祝休み、2026年8月16〜19日休み、夜のチャージ550円、夜は会計12,000円以下なら現金のみ、30席 (テーブル)、貸切50名まで、店内禁煙、子ども・ベビーカー可、ベジタリアンメニューあり。店の紹介: 1968年創業、六本木の路地裏の老舗、和をベースにした多国籍料理、35年続いた昼の営業は2024年12月20日で終了。口コミ(2025年3月〜2026年3月): 豆腐ステーキ、鮪の生姜焼き、チーズをのせた洋風餃子、ポリネシアンポーク、しらすと胡瓜のサラダ、牡蠣めし、タイカレー、和牛の鉄板焼き、昭和のプリン、テーブルのメニューに自分で注文を書く、店名の由来。

cultural_comfort.note: Menu written on the tables; you write down your own order.
